prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Database column specification for orders table (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Column" · longest unbreakable word 137px · one-line width 137px
  col 2: header "Type" · longest unbreakable word 99px · one-line width 210px
  col 3: header "Nullable" · longest unbreakable word 59px · one-line width 59px
  col 4: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 161px · one-line width 161px
  col 5: header "Comment" · longest unbreakable word 93px · one-line width 577px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 792px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 791px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A database schema reference for the orders table, used by developers/DBAs to verify column names, types, nullability, defaults, and meaning before querying or migrating.","reading":"Readers scan down the Column list to locate a field, then move horizontally across Type, Nullable, and Default to confirm its contract; the Comment is read last as explanation. Comparison happens primarily within columns, so identifiers and technical tokens should remain stable and easy to align.","groups":["Column, Type, Nullable, Default — the machine-readable schema contract, read together row by row","Comment — free-text human annotation, secondary to the schema facts and naturally wrappable"],"keep_intact":["order_id","customer_id","order_reference","status","total_amount_cents","currency_code","placed_at","cancelled_at","BIGINT UNSIGNED","VARCHAR(32)","VARCHAR(24)","INTEGER","CHAR(3)","TIMESTAMP","CURRENT_TIMESTAMP","NULL","'pending'","'USD'","YES/NO values"],"may_wrap":["Comment prose","Type phrases between words, such as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE","Longer comments can increase row height without harming the row’s meaning"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [158, 148, 80, 182, 223] · table 792×769px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 106, 106, 83, 83, 106, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [158, 140, 80, 182, 231] · table 792×699px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [158, 231, 80, 182, 140] · table 792×1141px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 153, 176, 129, 129, 153, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
